content: When the LORD appeared to young King Solomon in a dream, what did He say?
options: Ask, and I will give it
explanation: God offered Solomon any gift. “Ask, and I will give it to you!” (1 Kings 3:5, BSB)

content: In his dream, how did King Solomon describe himself to God?
explanation: He felt too young to rule. “But I am only a little child, not knowing how to go out or come in.” (1 Kings 3:7, BSB)

content: When God said “Ask,” what did King Solomon ask for?
explanation: He wanted to judge God's people well. “Therefore give Your servant an understanding heart to judge Your people” (1 Kings 3:9, BSB)

content: How did the Lord feel about King Solomon's request for wisdom?
explanation: Solomon did not ask selfishly. “Now it pleased the Lord that Solomon had made this request.” (1 Kings 3:10, BSB)

content: Besides wisdom, what did God also give King Solomon that he did not ask for?
explanation: God gave more than he asked. “Moreover, I will give you what you did not request—both riches and honor” (1 Kings 3:13, BSB)

content: When two women claimed the same baby, what did King Solomon order as a test?
explanation: The real mother would show herself. “Cut the living child in two and give half to one and half to the other.” (1 Kings 3:25, BSB)

content: How did King Solomon know who the baby's real mother was?
explanation: Her love for the child showed. “Give the living baby to the first woman. By no means should you kill him; she is his mother.” (1 Kings 3:27, BSB)

content: What did King Solomon plan to build for the Name of the LORD?
explanation: God had promised this to David. “So behold, I plan to build a house for the Name of the LORD my God” (1 Kings 5:5, BSB)

content: For the temple, what wood did King Solomon order from Lebanon?
explanation: Lebanon's cedars were famous. “Now therefore, order that cedars of Lebanon be cut down for me.” (1 Kings 5:6, BSB)

content: While Solomon's temple was built, what tools were never heard there?
explanation: Stones were cut at the quarry. “so that no hammer or chisel or any other iron tool was heard in the temple while it was being built.” (1 Kings 6:7, BSB)

content: What did King Solomon overlay the whole inside of the temple with?
explanation: It was a glorious house for God. “So he overlaid with gold the whole interior of the temple” (1 Kings 6:22, BSB)

content: How many years did it take King Solomon to build the temple?
explanation: It was finished in every detail. “So he built the temple in seven years.” (1 Kings 6:38, BSB)

content: When Solomon's temple was dedicated, what filled the house of the LORD?
explanation: God's glory filled it. “the cloud filled the house of the LORD” (1 Kings 8:10, BSB)

content: At the temple's dedication, what did King Solomon say cannot contain God?
explanation: God is greater than any building. “Even heaven, the highest heaven, cannot contain You, much less this temple I have built.” (1 Kings 8:27, BSB)

content: What did the prophet Elijah tell King Ahab would not come for years?
explanation: Only at Elijah's word would it rain. “there will be neither dew nor rain in these years except at my word!” (1 Kings 17:1, BSB)

content: By the Brook of Cherith, which birds did God command to feed Elijah?
explanation: God cared for His prophet. “and I have commanded the ravens to feed you there.” (1 Kings 17:4, BSB)

content: What did the ravens bring Elijah each morning and evening?
explanation: He drank from the brook. “The ravens would bring him bread and meat in the morning and evening” (1 Kings 17:6, BSB)

content: Why did Elijah have to leave the Brook of Cherith?
explanation: There was no rain. “Some time later, however, the brook dried up because there had been no rain in the land.” (1 Kings 17:7, BSB)

content: After the brook dried up, who did God say would provide for Elijah?
explanation: She lived in Zarephath. “Behold, I have commanded a widow there to provide for you.” (1 Kings 17:9, BSB)

content: When Elijah asked for bread, what did the widow of Zarephath have left?
explanation: She planned a last meal for her son. “only a handful of flour in a jar and a little oil in a jug.” (1 Kings 17:12, BSB)

content: What happened to the widow's flour and oil after she fed Elijah?
explanation: God kept His word. “The jar of flour was not exhausted and the jug of oil did not run dry” (1 Kings 17:16, BSB)

content: On which mountain did Elijah challenge the prophets of Baal?
explanation: All Israel gathered there. “Now summon all Israel to meet me on Mount Carmel” (1 Kings 18:19, BSB)

content: On Mount Carmel, what did Elijah ask the people?
explanation: They had to choose between God and Baal. “How long will you waver between two opinions?” (1 Kings 18:21, BSB)

content: On Mount Carmel, Elijah said the true God would answer by what?
explanation: Baal's prophets agreed to the test. “The God who answers by fire, He is God.” (1 Kings 18:24, BSB)

content: When Baal's prophets called on Baal all morning, what happened?
explanation: Baal was not real. “But there was no sound, and no one answered” (1 Kings 18:26, BSB)

content: Before praying on Mount Carmel, what did Elijah have poured on the offering?
explanation: It made the miracle even greater. “Fill four waterpots and pour the water on the offering and on the wood.” (1 Kings 18:34, BSB)

content: When Elijah prayed on Mount Carmel, what fell from the LORD?
explanation: It burned up even the water. “Then the fire of the LORD fell and consumed the sacrifice” (1 Kings 18:38, BSB)

content: After the fire fell on Mount Carmel, what did the people shout?
explanation: They fell facedown. “The LORD, He is God! The LORD, He is God!” (1 Kings 18:39, BSB)

content: Which priest anointed Solomon as king?
explanation: The people shouted, “Long live King Solomon!” “Zadok the priest took the horn of oil from the tabernacle and anointed Solomon.” (1 Kings 1:39, BSB)

content: After King David died, who sat on his throne?
explanation: His kingdom was firmly established. “So Solomon sat on the throne of his father David, and his kingdom was firmly established.” (1 Kings 2:12, BSB)

content: Where did the LORD appear to Solomon in a dream?
explanation: God offered him any gift. “One night at Gibeon the LORD appeared to Solomon in a dream” (1 Kings 3:5, BSB)

content: After Solomon judged the two women's case, what did all Israel see in him?
explanation: They stood in awe. “for they saw that the wisdom of God was in him to administer justice.” (1 Kings 3:28, BSB)

content: Solomon's understanding was beyond measure, like what on the seashore?
explanation: God gave him great wisdom. “and understanding beyond measure, like the sand on the seashore.” (1 Kings 4:29, BSB)

content: How many proverbs did King Solomon compose?
explanation: His songs numbered a thousand and five. “Solomon composed three thousand proverbs” (1 Kings 4:32, BSB)

content: Why could the priests not minister when Solomon's temple was dedicated?
explanation: The cloud filled the house. “for the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD.” (1 Kings 8:11, BSB)

content: Which queen came to test Solomon with difficult questions?
explanation: She had heard of his fame. “Now when the queen of Sheba heard about the fame of Solomon” (1 Kings 10:1, BSB)

content: When Solomon grew old, what turned his heart after other gods?
explanation: He was not fully devoted like David. “For when Solomon grew old, his wives turned his heart after other gods” (1 Kings 11:4, BSB)

content: Which king of Israel did more evil than all before him and opposed Elijah?
explanation: He was the son of Omri. “However, Ahab son of Omri did evil in the sight of the LORD, more than all who were before him.” (1 Kings 16:30, BSB)

content: When Elijah prayed for the widow's son who had died, what happened?
explanation: The LORD listened to Elijah. “and the child’s life returned to him, and he lived.” (1 Kings 17:22, BSB)

content: On Mount Carmel, what did Elijah say Baal might be doing?
explanation: He was mocking the false god. “Perhaps he is sleeping and must be awakened!” (1 Kings 18:27, BSB)

content: On Mount Carmel, how many stones did Elijah use to build the altar?
explanation: One for each tribe. “And Elijah took twelve stones, one for each tribe of the sons of Jacob” (1 Kings 18:31, BSB)

content: After Carmel, how big was the first cloud Elijah's servant saw rising from the sea?
explanation: Then heavy rain fell. “There is a cloud as small as a man’s hand rising from the sea.” (1 Kings 18:44, BSB)

content: When Elijah fled and slept under a broom tree, who woke him?
explanation: The angel told him to eat. “Suddenly an angel touched him and said, “Get up and eat.”” (1 Kings 19:5, BSB)

content: At the mountain of God, after wind, earthquake, and fire, what came to Elijah?
explanation: God spoke gently. “And after the fire came a still, small voice.” (1 Kings 19:12, BSB)

content: In what year after leaving Egypt did Solomon begin building the temple?
explanation: It was Solomon's fourth year. “In the four hundred and eightieth year after the Israelites had come out of the land of Egypt” (1 Kings 6:1, BSB)

content: How many cubits long, wide, and high was the temple's inner sanctuary?
explanation: It was a perfect cube of gold. “The inner sanctuary was twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and twenty cubits high.” (1 Kings 6:20, BSB)

content: Solomon said no one was as skilled in logging as which people?
explanation: They cut the cedars of Lebanon. “for you know that there are none among us as skilled in logging as the Sidonians.” (1 Kings 5:6, BSB)

content: How many songs did King Solomon write?
explanation: He also wrote 3,000 proverbs. “and his songs numbered a thousand and five.” (1 Kings 4:32, BSB)

content: Where was the prophet Elijah from?
explanation: He is called Elijah the Tishbite. “Now Elijah the Tishbite, who was among the settlers of Gilead” (1 Kings 17:1, BSB)

content: By which brook did Elijah hide during the drought?
explanation: It was east of the Jordan. “hide yourself by the Brook of Cherith, east of the Jordan.” (1 Kings 17:3, BSB)

content: In which town did the widow who fed Elijah live?
explanation: God sent him there. “Get up and go to Zarephath of Sidon, and stay there.” (1 Kings 17:9, BSB)

content: How many prophets of Baal faced Elijah on Mount Carmel?
explanation: Elijah stood alone. “along with the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal” (1 Kings 18:19, BSB)

content: Under what kind of tree did Elijah sit and pray to die?
explanation: He was worn out and afraid. “He sat down under a broom tree and prayed that he might die.” (1 Kings 19:4, BSB)

content: Strengthened by the angel's food, how long did Elijah walk to Horeb?
explanation: Horeb is the mountain of God. “he walked forty days and forty nights until he reached Horeb, the mountain of God.” (1 Kings 19:8, BSB)

content: In which month was Solomon's temple finished?
explanation: It was the eighth month. “In his eleventh year and eighth month, the month of Bul, the temple was finished” (1 Kings 6:38, BSB)
